brief.summary_1line: Rama orders Lakshmana to secretly leave Sita near Valmiki’s hermitage, and Lakshmana sorrowfully takes her toward the Ganges while hiding the truth.

image_candidates.scene_text: Lakshmana, eyes downcast with grief, helps the joyful and unsuspecting Sita climb into a richly cushioned chariot outside the palace.
Sita in the chariot on the road to the Ganges, touching her twitching eye and speaking anxiously of ominous signs while Lakshmana listens silently in anguish.
At dawn by a quiet riverside hermitage near the Ganges, Lakshmana stands beside the chariot, burdened with sorrow as the journey toward Sita’s abandonment continues.

deep.rich_summary: Rama, torn by duty and public opinion, orders Lakshmana to take the pregnant Sita away from Ayodhya and abandon her beyond the Ganges near the hermitage of the sage Valmiki. He forbids argument and insists the command be carried out immediately, even swearing that anyone who tries to change his decision will be treated as an enemy. Lakshmana, grief‑stricken but obedient, prepares a luxurious chariot with the charioteer Sumantra and tells Sita they are fulfilling her earlier wish to visit the forest hermitages by the Ganges. Delighted, Sita gathers jewels and garments to give to ascetics’ wives. As they travel, however, she begins to sense ominous signs—twitching eye, trembling limbs, and a growing unease—while Lakshmana hides his anguish. The journey toward the Ganges quietly sets the stage for one of the epic’s most tragic separations.

highlight_spans.why: Rama’s command that Lakshmana take Sita away begins the pivotal exile that defines the Uttara Kanda.
Rama withdraws in tears after issuing the order, revealing the painful conflict between royal duty and personal love.
Lakshmana deceives Sita gently by saying they are visiting the hermitages of sages along the Ganges.
Sita joyfully prepares gifts for ascetics’ wives, unaware she is being led into abandonment.
Sita senses ominous signs—twitching eye and trembling limbs—foreshadowing the tragic revelation soon to come.

top_scenes.scene_text: Lakshmana drives a royal chariot carrying Sita away from Ayodhya at dawn, his face grief‑stricken while she looks hopeful, the city fading behind them.
Sita in the chariot holding jewels and fine garments meant as gifts for ascetics’ wives, smiling while Lakshmana looks away in silent anguish.
The chariot halts near the misty banks of the Ganges beside a quiet forest hermitage, ominous stillness surrounding Sita as she senses bad omens.
